Both skills are in place. Let me reflect on whether memory needs updating.

The relative-difference convention is already in memory ("RELATIVE diff"=(A-B)/base*100, base=EARLIER yr). My memory is at 93% capacity, so I should not add redundant entries. The new skill captures the savings-note-specific traps (numerator = redemptions, denominator = average outstanding, notes-vs-bonds line). The relative-difference trap is the failure mode, and that general fact is already memorialized.

Summary of reflection:

What went wrong: I answered 3.85 (the bare absolute gap between the two years' redemption rates) when the gold answer 17.69 was the RELATIVE difference — (rate_1981 − rate_1980)/rate_1980 × 100. The ~4.6x miss is the classic "relative vs absolute difference" trap applied to a percentage rate.

What I saved:
- New skill `officeqa-savings-bond-redemption-rate-avg-outstanding` — documents this distinct question family: per-calendar-year redemption rate = annual redemptions ÷ average amount outstanding (= (prior-year-end + year-end)/2), notes-vs-bonds line selection, where the data lives, and the dominant relative-difference failure mode with the exact 3.85-vs-17.69 example.
- Cross-reference added to the existing accrued-discount skill so future agents disambiguate "rate out of outstanding" from "accrued-discount share."

I did not touch memory — the relative-difference convention is already recorded there and memory is near capacity, so the savings-note specifics belong in the skill, not memory.
